name: Uber
look: Two-colour pill hierarchy on a white ground, sentence-case display at weight 700, and alternating white and black bands mid-page.

hero.title: Go anywhere with Wayfarer
hero.sub: Request a ride, hop in, and go. Fares quoted before you book, drivers paid transparently, and a receipt that itemises where the money went.

features.title: A fare you agreed to
features.sub: The number you see when you book is the number you pay, and the receipt shows how it was made up.

items.title: Upfront fares
items.body: Quoted before you confirm, held unless the route changes materially — and then you are asked.

items.title: Itemised receipts
items.body: Base fare, distance, time and fees broken out, including what the driver received.

items.title: Safety features
items.body: Trip sharing, an in-app emergency button and driver verification on every trip.

items.title: Options that differ
items.body: Cheaper shared rides, larger vehicles, and accessible options where available.

items.title: Schedule ahead
items.body: Book up to thirty days out with a driver assigned in advance for airport runs.

items.title: Works abroad
items.body: The same account in seventy countries, with local payment methods supported.

showcases.title: Earnings shown before you accept
showcases.body: Drivers see the fare, the pickup distance and the destination before accepting, rather than after. Transparency on the driver side is what makes transparency on the rider side credible.
points: Fare and destination shown before accepting
No penalty for declining a trip

showcases.title: Travel that reconciles itself
showcases.body: Company accounts with policy limits, automatic receipt capture and a monthly export that matches your expense system without anyone photographing anything.
points: Monthly export in your accounting format

testimonial.quote: The receipt showed what the driver was paid. I had assumed that number would never be published, and seeing it changed how I felt about the fare.
testimonial.name: Tolu Adeyinka

items.a: Yes, unless the route changes materially — an added stop or a significantly different destination. In that case you are asked to confirm a new fare rather than surprised by one.

items.q: What does the driver actually receive?
items.a: It is on your receipt. Publishing it was a deliberate choice; a fare split you cannot see is a fare split nobody trusts.

items.q: What happens if I feel unsafe?
items.a: Share your trip in one tap, or use the in-app emergency button which passes your live location to the local service. Every driver is verified before their first trip.
Yes, in seventy countries, with local payment methods and local pricing. There is no separate account to create when you land.

cta.title: Get where you are going
cta.sub: Fares quoted before you book, and a receipt that explains itself.

notes: A two-colour CTA hierarchy: black pill for primary, white pill for secondary, soft grey pill for tertiary and chips.
The pill is the single signature shape on every interactive element, except the tab toggle and the larger product cards.
Every headline is sentence case at weight 700. There is no all-caps display anywhere in this system.
Editorial illustrations of riders, drivers and cars are the only consistent decorative system — no gradients, no atmospherics.
The band rhythm alternates white feature card, black promo card, white feature card, black footer. The black bands appear mid-page, not only in the hero.
